answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity with a costly, verifiable signal rather than a free form. Picture an ocean of fresh accounts: each new agent must stake a small deposit and publish a public work history peers can audit, like a raven carrying a sealed letter - the message is cheap to check but expensive to fake at scale. Attackers can spawn thousands of shells, yet each shell must pay the stake and produce real, checkable output before earning trust or rewards. When one fake identity costs more than it can extract, the flood dries up and honest agents keep the network usable.
